title: Playing at Bay St. Louis and closing remarks about his wife
summary: He talks of his band at a Bay St. Louis hotel, a boss who held his pay for his wife, and his two marriages; the tape ends.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well, you're just about out of tape. Is there anything else that you can think of about your life that you'd want to tell us? If not, why we can...

Well, I'm going to tell you, I come up the hard way and I got my music and I went and played this band, I'll tell you on the coast there, Auguste Associates. We used to play at the Reeds Hotel, you might know right at that light, there's one light.

Yeah, right about across. It's a light. Well we played there. And I used to get the drummer, he used to go out of town with me, George used to go with me, and I used to send Albert Fernandez, you know him? Yeah. I used to send him over there. Yeah. I'd send him over there and play in my place sometimes. I had to go fulfill my job somewhere, like Mobile somewhere, I had to go and play. So we made good money on that coast. But see, O.G. Associates, every night I played over there, he wouldn't give me a nickel. See, when I get ready to come home, give me the whole thing, huh? Yeah. Pee right now.
Yeah, he wouldn't let me spend nothing, you see?

I wouldn't spend something, he wouldn't let me. I'm telling you, you go bring this money home to Miss Lucia. That's what he'd take. Yeah, I had a fine wife, she's dead. I married again, I got another fine wife. You see that? Yeah. You ever been to him? Yeah.
Yeah, I knew you, I'd be very much, very fine wife. Well I think that looks like the end of it there. Alright, you spell it. Wrap her up. Wrap her up.
